_meta_itemized.notes: Christopher F. Robinson, County Council Seat D, 2014 Post-Election. THE GRAIN QUESTION IS SETTLED ON THE DOCUMENT'S OWN FACE, not by inference: page 4 is a scanned EMAIL from the filer to County Clerk Kent Jones, sent 2014-11-23 and stamped 'RECEIVED NOV 24 2014 SUMMIT COUNTY CLERK', which states 'My report prior to the election will in reality be my final report since I had no further contributions or expenditures after that.' The Post-Election filing is therefore the Pre-Election workbook re-filed unchanged, its Current-Report column IS its cumulative position, and both ledgers are cumulative-complete for the cycle. That also explains the cover, whose CUMULATIVE column is empty and whose Current Report column carries the figures the module promoted - the promotion rule and the filer's own statement agree. SOURCE PROPERTIES: (1) The filer did NOT use the county's blank form - he rebuilt it in Excel (footer 'CFR County Council Seat D Disclosure 10 27 2014.xls', 'Date Printed: 10/26/14', 'Page 2 of 3' / 'Page 3 of 3'), so there are no printed specimen rows to drop, and each schedule carries an EXTRA in-table 'Total' row that is a printed subtotal, not a transaction (contributions band 38, expenditures band 10) - both excluded, both used as gates. (2) The first contribution row is not a donor at all: it is the 'Beginning Balance Brought Forward from 2012 House District 54 Campaign' of $611.38, itemized by the filer inside the contribution schedule with 'n/a' in the address and zip cells, and it IS part of the printed $2,612.88. Retained verbatim as the form records it, flagged in its row note. (3) The last contribution row is a CAMPAIGN LOAN from the candidate to his own campaign ($301.50), also counted in the printed total. (4) A p3 purpose cell is TRUNCATED by the spreadsheet's column width - 'Reimbursement for Use of Temple Har Shalom for' ends mid-sentence; retained verbatim, never completed. (5) Addresses are printed in full and unredacted (2014 sheets are not county-redacted); only city/state are retained per the privacy contract. Teresa Beck's cell prints 'Salt Lake City' with NO state token, so her donor_state is honestly blank - a zip is never turned into a place. (6) Two of the donors are Park City municipal figures (Andy Beerman, later Park City's mayor; Robert Hilder) - noted only as context, never joined here. GEOMETRY: MEASURED on both pages. p3's rules and column rules detect cleanly (13 bands, 5 column rules) and the 6 rows sit in bands 3-8; verified by render-back - band 4 resolves to the two-line '10/3/14 Corrie Forsling / Reimbursement for my portion of Democratic Candidates Door Hangers / $176.00' row and band 8 to '10/27/14 Park Record / Newspaper Ads / $301.50'. p2 detects NO column rules and its band list is contaminated (39 bands, because this sheet's typed lines are wide enough to register as rules at the adaptive threshold), so the record supplies the table's own x/w (10.5 / 81.0, measured off the page) and each row is pointed at the detected band that CONTAINS its transaction line; all eight were validated by render-back (band 16 = Hilder $200.00, band 20 = the two-line Wangsgard row $500.00, band 27 = Beck $300.00, band 30 = the two-line Beerman row $250.00, band 34 = the two-line Campaign Loan row $301.50). ONE HONEST LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: the Parsons Behle & Latimer row is THREE printed lines tall and no single detected band spans it - band 25 (the box stored) contains the date, the name's third line, the zip and the $200.00, while the firm's name begins one band higher (24). SOURCE PROPERTY THE CONTRACT DID NOT ANTICIPATE: this page's rows are VARIABLE HEIGHT (1 to 4 text lines), so no uniform table_frame (y0 + pitch, one height for every band) can contain them - a numeric search over pitch 1.98-9.00 and every anchor returns no solution. That is why the rows use measured band indices rather than a declared frame here.
